components.gap: ED26-P15-CH-independent-random-variables-C004 partial: a justificatory claim in the required Durrett extent is omitted. In the held author Version 5 (source/references/durrett-probability-2019-01-11/PTE5_011119.pdf), the Remark printed directly after the proof of Theorem 2.1.7 (p. 47, PDF p. 55) states that for the class L = {A : P(A cap F) = P(A)P(F)} used in that proof it is not easy to show that A, B in L implies A cap B in L or A cup B in L, whereas A, B in L with A subset B easily gives B - A in L; this is why the argument goes through lambda-systems and the pi-lambda theorem. The route nowhere states it: thm:p15-independence-generators (handbook/parts/p15/independent-random-variables.tex lines 108-121) only names the pi-lambda theorem; annex:p15.independence-generators (handbook/annex/p15/independent-random-variables.tex lines 92-158) verifies only the lambda-system properties of L_D (lines 115-139); def:p15-pi-lambda and thm:p15-measure-uniqueness (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 400-415) and their proof carry no such remark. Supply this remark for L_D on the route from the packet's editable host or owned files: L_D contains Omega and is closed under proper differences and increasing unions, but need not be closed under intersections or unions (witness: in the four-point model of item 2 of thm:p15-independence-counterexamples, A and B lie in L_C while A cap B and A cup B do not), which is why the pi-lambda theorem, not a direct sigma-algebra argument, is applied.
